answer.rationale:
memory_c2 is the load-bearing memory here: it is the only record asserting that the low-cost vendor can absorb primary volume cleanly, and the entire case for a full switch rests on it. I want the original record because the consolidated summary hides exactly the details that decide this cycle - which component, what share of volume, whether the line had buffer at the time, and whether 'quick onboarding' meant weeks or a quarter. A cheap quote plus a favorable summary from a prior year is not evidence that this vendor holds up at 94% committed volume with no buffer and 14 days to cutover.

The two constraints point in opposite directions. Finance's 18% mandate and the incumbent's refusal to reopen price (which makes memory_c4's renegotiation play unavailable this cycle, and memory_c1/memory_c6's renewal comfort unaffordable) push toward the low-cost vendor. The 94% utilization with no buffer and a hard 14-day expiry pushes against a single-source cutover to a vendor unproven at this volume - that is the configuration where a two-week slip becomes a line stoppage, and stoppage cost swamps 18% of component spend. defer_decision is not safe either, since the contract does not auto-renew; memory_c5's deferral worked on a non-critical, month-to-month service, not on primary supply feeding a saturated line.

So: qualify the low-cost vendor as a second source at a guarded share now, with the incumbent carrying the balance on a short bridge, per memory_c3's dual-sourcing result under constraint. This captures partial savings immediately and buys the performance data that would justify a full primary shift at the next review, without betting the line on one archived summary.

Downstream value risk, stated plainly: this will likely not deliver the full 18% this year. I am consciously trading part of the mandate for delivery integrity, and finance should see that tradeoff rather than discover it. Second risk: a partial award may forfeit the low-cost vendor's volume pricing and may harden the incumbent's stance, so the bridge terms should be short and the next-review decision genuinely open. If the archived record for memory_c2 shows that switch was at comparable volume, on this component, with a proven ramp, I will escalate to a full switch_primary_vendor this cycle instead.
